problem_statement: The syscon register interface has two gaps. First, there is no way to atomically read-modify-write a subset of a register's bits: a caller cannot clear and set specific bit positions in a single, lock-protected operation, so concurrent accessors can race on a separate read followed by a write. Second, a register offset that is not a multiple of the register's byte width is silently rounded down to the nearest aligned offset instead of being rejected, so a caller requesting an out-of-alignment offset reads or writes the wrong register with no error reported.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_cortex_a53 -T tests/drivers/syscon -s tests/drivers/syscon/drivers.syscon -s drivers.syscon -O twister-out --no-clean -W
